My review after playing it for 2 hours as a QA analyst Gameplay & UX Analysis Overall Rating: 7/10 Vacation Cafe Simulator delivers an engaging core loop with strong progression and co-op potential, making it fun for short sessions and restaurant management fans. The unlock system keeps players motivated, but polish issues in UI, optimization, AI, and repetition hold it back from feeling complete. What Works Well Strong Core Loop & Progression The restaurant management and expansion systems are addictive – new recipes, purchases, and space upgrades provide constant motivation. Standout Mechanics — Satisfying progression (new recipes per level, restaurant expansion) — Co-op potential feels promising for chaotic, fun sessions — Basic mini-games provide quick satisfaction Key Improvement Areas 1. Lobby UI Clarity Observation: "Create Lobby" image is noticeably blurred compared to the "Join" image. Impact: Creates visual inconsistency and confusion during multiplayer setup. Recommendation: Match image quality/clarity across all lobby options for professional polish. 2. Optimization & Input Lag (High Priority) Observation: Mouse feels delayed, with occasional image stutters. Impact: Breaks flow during busy service periods, frustrating fast-paced mini-games and customer interactions. Recommendation: Optimize input responsiveness and frame stability – target 60fps minimum with reduced stutter. 3. Time Indication (Medium Priority) Observation: No visible hours or time display (only sunlight level). Impact: Players lose track of day/night cycles, affecting planning for peak hours or closures. Recommendation: Add prominent clock/hours UI in top bar or HUD for better time awareness. 4. AI Animations & Player Collision (High Priority) Observation: AI animations are sluggish; collision with other players feels off. Impact: Causes awkward overlaps and movement frustration, especially in co-op. Recommendation: Smooth AI pathing/animations and improve player collision detection for fluid interactions. 5. Music Repetition (Medium Priority) Observation: Music loops with only 2 tracks maximum. Impact: Becomes repetitive during longer sessions, reducing immersion. Recommendation: Add more tracks or dynamic variation (e.g. day/night themes, busier music during peak hours). 6. Mini-Game Variety (Medium Priority) Observation: Most mini-games are repetitive "left click repeat" mechanics. Impact: Reduces engagement after initial novelty wears off. Recommendation: Introduce variation (timing challenges, patterns, combos) to keep mini-games fresh. 7. NPC Collision (Medium Priority) Observation: No collision with NPCs – players can see their "buggy insides" and clip through. Impact: Breaks immersion and causes visual glitches during service. Recommendation: Add proper collision bounds and hide internal models. 8. Order Persistence After Closure (Critical) Observation: Customer order disappears after closing restaurant; customer remains seated indefinitely and won't order again, even after reopening. Impact: Softlock on customer progression, wasting table space and frustrating flow. Recommendation: Persist orders across closures or auto-clear/leave seated customers after timeout. Final Assessment Vacation Cafe Simulator has a compelling loop with addictive progression and strong co-op potential that could shine with polish. The foundation is solid, but optimization, UI clarity, AI responsiveness, and repetition need attention to elevate it from promising demo to engaging experience. Addressing these would make it much more enjoyable for solo and multiplayer sessions. Even though it needs a bit of polish here and there I still had a blast playing it with the wife! Can't wait to play the full game when it releases! For more reviews check: https://sites.google.com/view/qaportfolio-fanas/home

Hi , sorry for the late feedback for this but I do feel it is the most important thing that keeps the game from feeling authentic italian inspired The pizza dough recipe is too different from reality. Pizza dough is made with just flour, water and yeast and salt. There is no milk and eggs in it at all. Milk and eggs are for sweet dough. My suggestion would be to change the recipe to make a water carafe in the mixing table that works like the olive oil bottle; as in it's part of the table itself and you would use it for the mixing. You could add fresh yeast cubes to the fridge as a purchasable ingredient in the store but honestly it's okay to not even add it and just ignore it for the sake of gameplay. The important thing is to not have eggs and milk in the recipe. I understand it might feel like a minor issue but it really does take me out of the experience; it's a completely different recipe

The village in the game is very beautiful, and I hope the full game directs players to explore most of it. I have explored a lot of it on my own, and it is much, much bigger than I thought it would be. So, I hope the full release gives you more shops and more relaxing things to do--even things that don't have to anything to do with the cafe. For example. It would be nice to have a night cafe in the village that you do not own, but you can go there and relax, maybe order a Benedictine or Limoncello or Amaretto, sit on a porch, and watch the sunset. Or to have a shop where you can buy different cat collars or cat beds or cat bowls, and customize the cat outside the restaurant. Maybe give him a little umbrella too, which he will ignore because cats like the sun. Maybe you can buy a tropical fish and put him in a glass tank as a decoration to the restaurant. Or to have a building that's the center for promoting tourism. If you pay to advertise your cafe in their magazine, ships of tourists come to shore and wander around the town, maybe even ending up in your cafe as clients. Or there's a cycling race that ends at your village, and a bunch of cyclists come to your cafe with their bikes, and order water and carbs. One more idea: It would be nice to customize the streetlights outside of the restaurant. Although expensive, the night lighting might create a kind of vibe you want to go for, or it might attract more customers after midnight. Optimization? qc [VAC], TC

Demo feedback; enjoyable and a good start but it is jank Honestly I liked immediately the vibe of the old town; it feels really homely and reminds me a lot of games like "on your tail" in terms of environment. Not sure if the devs are Italian or visited Italy but it is a good approximation of an Italian small village. The game is fun to play; a bit easy maybe as there is no "patience" bar that goes down if you don't serve customers, so I would like to see an option to set that so each player can set their experience as they want (just add the option to have a timer or not for customers). Cooking is fun, a bit convoluted when you need to prepare multiple dishes though, as you cannot carry too many things or prepare things in advance. If I know I need to cut cheese because cheese is always cut for the recipe, would be nice to have an option where I can cut 10 cheese of each type and put them in a bin in the fridge. Or prepare ahead of time some dishes and refrigerate them (the game has no issues with me serving sparkling wine sitting on a table in a glass for a day). Buying stuff at the stores is great; not realistic to leave customers there and the shop open while you go buy stuff but it is OK :) Notice that you can just walk away with food in your basket without pay, that seems a bug to me. There is a lot of jank but it is understandable as this is a demo. Hopefully you polish animations and interactions in the final game. Curious to see what you do outside the village area, I saw some vespa mopeds for rent at one point and would be nice to have some gameplay where you drive over some other places outside the limited village, or even do deliveries of food for example. Interesting game, really relaxing and enjoyable so far. Looking forward to see what else will you add in the final game. The graphic style and art is probably the highlight here.
